e-7345.knowledge_point: Finding the Real or Imaginary Part of a Scalar Given the Conjugate of a Scaled Vector
e-7345.worked_solution:
Since $\overline{k\mathbf{v}} = \overline{k} \, \overline{\mathbf{v}},$ we get the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{kv} & =\overset{―}{k}\,\overset{―}{v} \\ [\begin{aligned}8\text{i}-12 \\ 0\end{aligned}] & =\overset{―}{k}\,\overset{―}{[\begin{aligned}-4\text{i} \\ 0\end{aligned}]} \\ [\begin{aligned}8\text{i}-12 \\ 0\end{aligned}] & =\overset{―}{k}\,[\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{-4\text{i}} \\ \overset{―}{0}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}8\text{i}-12 \\ 0\end{aligned}] & =\overset{―}{k}\,[\begin{aligned}4\text{i} \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}8\text{i}-12 \\ 0\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}4\text{i}\,\overset{―}{k} \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, we obtain that 

$$
4\textrm{i}\,\overline{k}  = 8\textrm{i}-12
\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
\overline{k}=\dfrac{8\textrm{i}-12}{4\textrm i} = 2+3\textrm{i}.
$$

 

Therefore, $k=\overline{2+3\textrm{i}}=2-3\textrm{i}.$

Finally, $\textrm{Im}(k)=-3.$

after.worked_solution:
To find the complex conjugate of a vector, we take the complex conjugate of the entries of the vector. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\overset{―}{x}}_{2} & =\overset{―}{[\begin{aligned}-6\text{i} \\ 1+2\text{i}\end{aligned}]} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{-6\text{i}} \\ \overset{―}{1+2\text{i}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6\text{i} \\ 1-2\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Multiplying the second vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{i}\cdot {\overset{―}{x}}_{2} & =\text{i}\cdot [\begin{aligned}6\text{i} \\ 1-2\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6{\text{i}}^{2} \\ \text{i}-2{\text{i}}^{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 2+\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+\text{i}\cdot {\overset{―}{x}}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}3-8\text{i} \\ -4+2\text{i}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 2+\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3-8\text{i} \\ -2+3\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

To find the complex conjugate of a vector, we take the complex conjugate of the entries of the vector. So, we have

x―2=[−6i1+2i]―=[−6i―1+2i―]=[6i1−2i].

Multiplying the second vector, we get

i⋅x―2=i⋅[6i1−2i]=[6i2i−2i2]=[−62+i].

Therefore, x1+i⋅x―2=[3−8i−4+2i]+[−62+i]=[−3−8i−2+3i].

content.worked_solution:
To find the complex conjugate of a vector, we take the complex conjugate of the entries of the vector. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\overset{―}{x}}_{2} & =\overset{―}{[\begin{aligned}-6\text{i} \\ 1+2\text{i}\end{aligned}]} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{-6\text{i}} \\ \overset{―}{1+2\text{i}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6\text{i} \\ 1-2\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Multiplying the second vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{i}\cdot {\overset{―}{x}}_{2} & =\text{i}\cdot [\begin{aligned}6\text{i} \\ 1-2\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6{\text{i}}^{2} \\ \text{i}-2{\text{i}}^{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 2+\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+\text{i}\cdot {\overset{―}{x}}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}3-8\text{i} \\ -4+2\text{i}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 2+\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3-8\text{i} \\ -2+3\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

$$

decision.explanation: Complex conjugation reverses the sign of each imaginary part and leaves real parts unchanged. Thus 9−6i becomes 9+6i, 9−3i becomes 9+3i, and −3 remains −3, matching option e.

after.worked_solution:
To find the complex conjugate of a vector, we take the complex conjugate of the entries of the vector. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\overset{―}{[\begin{aligned}9-6\text{i} \\ 9-3\text{i} \\ -3\end{aligned}]} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{9-6\text{i}} \\ \overset{―}{9-3\text{i}} \\ \overset{―}{-3}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}9+6\text{i} \\ 9+3\text{i} \\ -3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
For the given vector $\,v=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 7\text{i}-4\end{aligned}]\,$ we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 7\text{i}-4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3+0\text{i} \\ -4+7\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -4\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Re}(v)}+\text{i}\,{{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 7\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{\text{Im}(v)}.\end{aligned}
$$
